messages:
jen_support: FYI — after rolling v3.2.1 to a 60% canary, Acme and two other customers report toolcall failures (HTTP 400 schema errors). Putting logs and repro below.
alex_oncall: grabbing logs now. which endpoint? exec API or SDK?
jen_support: exec API /v1/exec -> tool "lookup_weather". Sample error: "toolcall schema validation failed: missing required field 'user_timezone'". Customer says this used to work on v3.2.0.
dan_ml: I see a pattern in canary traces — v3.2.1 is preferring a newer tool variant lookup_weather_v2 which has a stricter schema. We added that variant to improve disambiguation but apparently didn't preserve backward compat.
sophia_prod: Can we pause or rollback the canary? How big is the error spike?
alex_oncall: Error rate for toolcall paths up ~6% at 60% canary (spike started ~2478121200). Latency P95 for those calls also up ~120ms. I'll collect traces and ids.
carlos_cs: Customer oncall mentioned retry loops causing elevated billing — they saw repeated 400->client retries. Need to reduce customer impact ASAP.
jen_support: Pasting a sanitized request/response from Acme:
```
POST /v1/exec
{
  "model": "redwood-inference-3.2.1",
  "tool": "lookup_weather",
  "args": {
    "location": "NYC",
    "units": "metric"
  }
}

HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
{
  "error": "schema_validation",
  "message": "missing required field 'user_timezone' for tool lookup_weather_v2"
}
```
acme_user: Confirming — same request worked yesterday on v3.2.0. No timezone field was required before.
dan_ml: Reproducer verified in staging when switching to model v3.2.1 default: new JSON schema enforced. This is an onboarding bug: the tool variant selector is returning v2 variant for certain prompt patterns.
alex_oncall: Short-term mitigation options:
- Rollback canary to v3.2.0 (fast, kills the regression)
- Add server-side compatibility layer to coerce missing timezone to account default (less disruption for customers)
- Add fallback routing rule to prefer lookup_weather_v1 for now
I'm leaning rollback + compatibility patch.
sophia_prod: Rollback + patch sounds right. We need impact assessment and comms. Sales/CS must be notified for affected accounts.
ops_bot: Rollback plan triggered by ops. Starting canary rollback from v3.2.1 -> v3.2.0 at 15:12 UTC. Watch deployments: https://deploys.redwood.example/ops/rollback/2478123456
jen_support: I'll update the affected customers and open an incident ticket with remediation ETA.
acme_user: Appreciate the quick response. Repro steps we used:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/exec \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-inference-3.2.1","tool":"lookup_weather","args":{"location":"NYC","units":"metric"}}'
```
Expect: tool response JSON { temperature, conditions }
Observed: 400 schema error requiring user_timezone.
```
dan_ml: I'll add a quick compatibility shim in the serving layer to inject account timezone when missing. That plus rollback should be enough to stop customer retries from billing them.
alex_oncall: Creating a short-lived routing rule to prefer v1 for lookup_weather while patch rolls out. Also removing strict rejection for unknown optional fields for 24h window.
sophia_prod: Please prepare a short postmortem template: root cause (tool variant selection + schema change), mitigations (rollback, compat shim), action items (add model/tool integration test, add canary validation for tool schema drift), and customer comms.
carlos_cs: I'll coordinate customer updates and ask legal if any billing credits are needed for Acme.
jen_support: Filed support ticket INC-24781235 and added customers. Will post status updates here. :thumbsup:
ops_bot: Rollback complete to v3.2.0 at 15:27 UTC. Monitoring for error spike to return to baseline.
alex_oncall: Error rate back to baseline on toolcall paths. Leaving the compatibility shim PR in draft for review: https://git.redwood/infra/compat-shim/pull/42
sophia_prod: Thanks team. After the postmortem let's add a canary checklist item: validate tool schema compatibility across existing customers before promoting variants.
